chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Above every person of righteousness is a [more meritorious] righteous deed, until he is killed in the Way of Allah. So when he is killed in the Way of Allah, there is no righteous deed above it.'

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: The Way of Allah (often referring to jihad or striving in God's cause)

ai.seo_question: What is the highest merit in Islam according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi outlines a cumulative hierarchy of virtues, emphasizing that while martyrdom represents the ultimate sacrifice, it is the culmination of a life dedicated to righteousness. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to highlight that the martyr's status is not merely due to the moment of death, but is the final seal on a lifetime of 'birr' (righteousness), distinguishing true martyrs from those who die without prior piety. The hadith thus serves as both an encouragement for striving in Allah's path and a reminder that martyrdom is the reward for sustained devotion.
